items.title: Henry "Pickle" Jackson Interview, 1961-08-09
items.q: Joe Newman was a hometown boy, played around here with us.

ctx.x: I never did get to hear it. I might have heard the band once. Oh, 1942 or something. When I first was around here. But how did it compare? I mean, it might be difficult for you to judge yourself if you were playing in it. But how did it compare, say, with Count Basie or Lunsford or some of those other big bands? Did it seem as powerful and as big as... Well, at the time...

How did it compare, do you think? At the time, I think the band compared as powerful as Count Basie's band at the time because they had a lot of young musicians in it and a lot of good ones. And they could play. They could blow. And to me, the musician was just as good as any musician you could find anywhere in the world. Just as good as musicians you could find in Count Basie. Maybe Basie might have been playing a different type of music. Or might have been playing a little fast or something like that. But as…
See, Earl Bostic, the saxophonist, did he ever play with you or with Sidney Diasbeen or other groups? I know he was here for a while.
